executive_summary: This collection window (July 21-27, 2026) falls in a genuine off-season lull: no runway/fashion-week event occurred during this period (Paris Couture and Men's wrapped in late June/early July; the next major show, Copenhagen Fashion Week SS27, does not open until August), and targeted web search surfaced only recycled seasonal-roundup content (generic 'summer trends,' 'back-to-school' pieces) rather than dated, verifiable discourse specific to this window. Two items previously logged as active signals -- the Chanel/Charvet acquisition and the 'Off-Duty Varsity' World Cup jersey-styling signal -- were checked for continuation. Charvet coverage has fully quieted (no new trade-press follow-up found this window, consistent with a completed, already-reported acquisition rather than an ongoing discourse signal). The jersey-styling signal's post-tournament check (recommended in the July 20 report, since the 2026 FIFA World Cup ended July 19) also came up empty: no dated coverage from this window was found reframing jersey styling outside the tournament occasion, which is itself weak evidence for the declining/event-driven reading rather than a durable style shift, but is not strong enough on its own to log as a fresh finding. Per the project's honesty-over-quota principle (see thin-week fallback guidance), this report is marked 'thin' rather than padded with repackaged seasonal-roundup copy to hit a target signal count.

top_signals.name: "Off-Duty Varsity" jersey styling, post-tournament check
top_signals.evidence: Following the July 20, 2026 report's flag to re-check this signal after the 2026 FIFA World Cup closed (June 11-July 19), a targeted search this window for post-tournament jersey-styling coverage returned only pieces published during the tournament itself (Who What Wear's 'How to Style a Soccer Jersey for the World Cup,' The Zoe Report's jersey-styling piece, Complex's styling guide) -- no editorial or retail source was found this window reframing soccer-jersey styling as a standalone, tournament-independent wardrobe habit.
top_signals.index_note: Absence of new post-tournament coverage is treated as weak corroborating evidence for the 'event-driven search noise' reading flagged in the prior two reports, not confirmation -- a search returning no new hits could equally reflect the general slowdown in fashion-press output this window rather than the signal's actual demise. Confidence held at low; volatility held at declining rather than downgraded to a terminal state, since one absent-evidence window is not sufficient to close the signal out.
top_signals.human_editor_note: This closes the loop the July 13 and July 20 reports opened, but on thin evidence (absence of hits, not a positive statement that jersey styling has stopped). A human editor should decide whether one more quiet window is enough to retire this signal_id from active tracking, or whether it should simply lapse from future reports without a formal close-out.

limitations: This was a genuinely low-output collection window: no fashion week or comparable industry event occurred July 21-27, 2026, and search results for this period were dominated by generic, undated 'summer 2026' and 'back-to-school 2026' roundup content rather than discourse specific to this window.

Several items considered for inclusion (Gymshark founder Ben Francis's stake buyback talks with General Atlantic, reported July 4, 2026; France's ultra-fast-fashion advertising-restriction law, passed by the French Senate June 29, 2026) were excluded because they fall outside this collection window and are business/regulatory news rather than style discourse.

The single logged signal (off-duty-varsity post-tournament check) is a continuation/close-out check on a signal first logged July 13, 2026, not a newly discovered signal this window; its evidence is an absence of new coverage, which is weaker than a positive finding and is flagged as such.
This report was assembled via targeted web search rather than a live automated crawl or direct social-platform API/dataset access, consistent with prior reports' compliant manual-sampling approach.
